editorial:
Imagine you are stepping back into 16th-century England, but instead of seeing kings and queens, you are looking at regular people with messy lives. You will meet Alice and her lover, Mosbie, who are tired of waiting for Alice's husband, Thomas Arden, to get out of the way. Their relationship is full of heat and tension, and they quickly decide that murder is the only way to be together. It feels like a dark domestic drama where the stakes are life and death, and the vibe is very tense as you watch them try to pull off a crime in a small town where everyone knows everyone.

What really works here is how the plan keeps falling apart. You will find yourself rooting for the tension to break as their clumsy attempts at murder fail one by one. The acting is solid, though the pacing can feel a bit slow in the middle since it is an older TV movie. If you enjoy old-school mysteries with a bit of a grit to them, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: After several failed attempts, the plot finally works when hired killers ambush Thomas Arden and kill him. However, the victory is short-lived. Alice and Mosbie are eventually caught because their lies stop adding up and the evidence points right at them. The movie ends with a sense of justice as the law catches up to the lovers, and they face the death penalty for their crimes, proving that their plan was doomed from the start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old crime dramas and historical mysteries.
